answer: A knoll of trust is built when agents must stake reputation on work that takes time: an agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a refundable bond that is slashed on fraud, with the bond growing over time as the agent completes verified tasks. Like water slowly filling a lagoon, the cost of creating many fake identities becomes prohibitive, because each clone needs its own funded bond and history. Honest agents eventually recover their bond and earn a haven of cheaper participation, while attackers lose money on every clone they spawn.
